Details of Kshethram:
Moolavar: Moovaragiya Oruvan
Thayaar: Vaikuntanayaki Thayaar
Vimanam: Sudhasatva Vimanam
Pushkarani: Sesha Theertham by Adiseshan and Vajra Theertham by Garudan

Travel: This kshethram is located 5 km from Cuddalore.

Azhwar Pasuram:
Tirumangai Azhwar: 10 pasuram

Sthala Puranam: 
Legend has it that a Deva-Asura Yudham once took place, and Lord Vishnu sided with the Devas, while Lord Shiva was said to have sided with the Asuras. When the battle raged in the dark, Lord Shiva is said to have hurled his Trishulam at Lord Vishnu, who responded by stopping the Trishulam with his Sudarshana Chakram. The Lord then showed Lord Shiva that He, Himself, was Lord Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. This is said to have humbled Lord Shiva.

***During the Krita Yugam, the rakshasas Madhu and Kaitabha stole the Vedas from Lord Brahma, and the Lord took the Matsya Avataram to recover them. The Lord then took the form of Hayagrivar and became the Lord of knowledge. Sriman Vedanta Desikan performed tapas here at Aushadagiri(the divine hill that was brought by Hanuman, containing the divine Sanjeevini), which is adjacent to the temple. Garudan is said to have been impressed by his tapas and appeared before Vedanta Desikan. Garudan then initiated the Hayagriva Stotram(see the picture above). Vedanta Desikan is then said to have meditated upon Lord Hayagriva by chanting the stotram. Lord Hayagriva then presented Vedanta Desikan with an idol of Himself, which is said to have been passed down through the lineage of various aradhakas, such as Devi Saraswati and Bhagavad Ramanuja, and is currently worshipped at the Parakala Muttam situated in Mysore. One who chants this stotram will attain proper knowledge of education, good concentration in studies, fluency in speech, mastery in debates, vocabulary, and will have outstanding memory power.
